title: The Murty–Simon conjecture on diameter-2-critical graphs
abstract: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the proof by Sanjana Das and Jacob Fox of the Murty–Simon conjecture (arXiv:2610.39032, 2026). A graph is diameter-2-critical if its diameter is 2 and deleting any edge increases the diameter. Theorem 1.1: every diameter-2-critical graph on n vertices has at most ⌊n²/4⌋ edges (murty_simon), and a diameter-2-critical graph with ⌊n²/4⌋ edges is isomorphic to K_{⌈n/2⌉,⌊n/2⌋} (murty_simon_equality). Also: for n ≥ 3, K_{⌈n/2⌉,⌊n/2⌋} is diameter-2-critical with ⌊n²/4⌋ edges, so the bound is attained (murty_simon_sharp); Lemma 1.2, |E(G) \ M| ≤ |non-edges of G| for every maximal matching M of a diameter-2-critical graph G (lemma_1_2); and Lemma 1.3, a diameter-2-critical graph with equality in Lemma 1.2 for every maximal matching is triangle-free (lemma_1_3). Five statements; the bound holds for every n, with no lower bound on n.
